summary: The English of 4:7-4:12 is faithful and consistent with Bartenura and Rambam throughout; the one change to a reading is 'a vain oath' for 'a false oath' in 4:7, which narrowed Bartenura's two readings to his second. The main faults are in the word analysis: many senses were taken mechanically from wrong homographs (place-names and proper names for עֶצֶם, דָּן, אָדָם, שָׂכָר, קָנָה, טוֹב, שֵׁם; 'falcon' for גַּס; 'where?' for אֵין; 'captain' for רַב), and nouns were given verb entries (עֹנִי, עֹשֶׁר, עֵסֶק, מִעֵט); these are re-pointed to the Jastrow entries the pack holds or their senses removed. In 4:7 the glosses of גַּס, לִבּוֹ and בַהוֹרָאָה were shifted by one word. Two Rambam summaries omitted the part bearing on the English, and the 4:12 chain note was false. The model morphology needed fixes to construct/absolute state (גַּס רוּחַ, מוֹרָא), the elided article after ב, the unsplit כִּתְרִיס, and the lemma and root of קִיֵּם.

patches.value: Rabbi Ishmael his son says: One who holds himself back from judging removes from himself enmity, robbery, and a vain oath. But one who is overbold of heart in giving rulings is a fool, wicked, and haughty of spirit.
patches.reason: 'A false oath' takes only Bartenura's second reading (a lying oath). His first reading, and Rabbeinu Yonah's שבועת חנם, is an oath imposed on one not liable to it: needless, not false. 'A vain oath' (שָׁוְא, 'emptiness, vanity') carries both.

Bartenura's second reading of בְטֵלִים, and Rabbeinu Yonah's 'bears and lions idle from work', both rest on the sense 'those who are idle'.
Rambam reads בְטֵלִים הַרְבֵּה as 'many things that make idle': affairs that demand attention and, if you leave the Torah, will occupy you.

value: יְהִי is the jussive of הָיָה: 'let ... be'.
The last two clauses form a chain: the 'reverence of your teacher' that ends the second clause begins the third; each clause sets one duty beside a higher one.
